content: Buprenorphine administered via the buccal route may have its levels or effects reduced due to the induction of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. Rifampin can decrease the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Patients on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require new treatment with CYP3A4 inducers should be monitored for withdrawal symptoms. If the dose of the CYP3A4 inducer cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should transition to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows for dose adjustments. If a CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued in a patient stabilized on buprenorphine, monitor for signs of overmedication. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal formulations by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are advised. If coadministration is necessary, consider increasing the buprenorphine transdermal dosage until stabilization is achieved. Monitor for opioid withdrawal symptoms. If the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, consider reducing the buprenorphine dosage and monitor for respiratory depression. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injections by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are necessary. Patients transitioning to buprenorphine long-acting injections from transmucosal buprenorphine coadministered with CYP3A4 inducers should be monitored to ensure adequate plasma levels. If the buprenorphine dose is inadequate and the CYP3A4 inducer cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of bupropion by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases butabarbital and butalbital levels by increasing their metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as they may decrease cabazitaxel concentrations. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of calcifediol and calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Drugs that stimulate microsomal hydroxylation reduce the half-life of calcifediol. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of rifampin by reducing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least one hour before antacids. Similarly, calcium/vitamin D reduces rifampin absorption; administer rifampin at least one hour before antacids. Rifampin decreases the levels of canagliflozin by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. For patients with an eGFR <73 mL/min/1.73 m², consider alternative antihyperglycemic agents. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Cannabidiol may also affect CYP2B6 metabolism, necessitating dosage adjustments of CYP2B6 substrates. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of carvedilol by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases caspofungin levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Cenobamate reduces rifampin levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Increase the dose of CYP2B6 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cevimeline, chlordiazepoxide, and chloroquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by decreasing its elimination. Avoid concomitant use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as this may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If concomitant use is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of citalopram by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clomipramine by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clonazepam and clorazepate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Clotrimazole increases rifampin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor patients. Concomitant use of cotrimoxazole increases rifampin concentrations, potentially increasing toxicity risk. Monitor for adverse reactions during coadministration. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clozapine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal) and cortisone by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases crizotinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while crizotinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by inducing CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases cyclosporine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Danicopan increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates; consider dose reductions of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Mipomersen and pyrazinamide may increase each other's toxicity due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs). Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dantrolene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases daprodustat levels by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitor hemoglobin levels and adjust daprodustat dosage when initiating or discontinuing CYP2C8 inducers. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dapsone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases daunorubicin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces deferasirox levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid concomitant use with potent UGT inducers. If coadministration is required, consider increasing the initial deferasirox dose to 30 mg/kg and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deflazacort and dexamethasone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases diazepam levels (buccal and intranasal) by inducing CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase diazepam elimination, reducing its efficacy. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces digoxin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of disopyramide, docetaxel, and dolutegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Increase dolutegravir dosage when coadministering with strong UGT1A/CYP3A4 inducers. Avoid rifampin in patients with integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-associated resistance, as concomitant use may result in therapeutic failure and resistance development. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of donepezil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxepin cream, doxorubicin, and doxorubicin liposomal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dronabinol by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of duvelisib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin reduces elafibranor levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Rifampin increases elagolix levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter but decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Limit concomitant use of elagolix 150 mg daily and rifampin to six months. Eliglustat increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates and titrate to clinical effect. Rifampin reduces eltrombopag levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Eltrombopag increases rifampin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. Encorafenib increases rifampin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. Encorafenib, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments of these substrates. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of enfortumab vedotin and eplerenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients.
